First, we express the given probability as

$$
P(|X|<3)=P(-3<X<3).
$$

Then, we find the cumulative probability using symmetry:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-3<X<3) & =0.5468 \\ 2P(0<X<3) & =0.5468 \\ P(0<X<3) & =0.2734 \\ P(X<3)-P(X<0) & =0.2734 \\ P(X<3)-0.5 & =0.2734 \\ P(X<3) & =0.7734 \\ P(X\le 3) & =0.7734\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 3) & =0.7734 \\ P(Z\le \frac{3-0}{\sigma }) & =0.7734 \\ Φ(\frac{3}{\sigma }) & =0.7734 \\ \frac{3}{\sigma } & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.7734)\end{aligned}
$$

According to the table, we have

$$
Φ(0.75)=0.7734\,⇒\,{Φ}^{-1}(0.7734)=0.75.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{\sigma } & =0.75 \\ \sigma  & =\frac{3}{0.75} \\ \sigma  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =(4)^{2}=16.\end{aligned}
$$
